findings.problem: Example 1 requires the negative-exponent rule, but Core Concept never explains that a negative exponent means a reciprocal. The rule is taught in Exponent Laws and Zero Powers, but this part does not identify that prerequisite. The student first encounters the required rule inside the solution.
findings.source: Content checklist L17 and L25; lesson-style-guide.md, Teaching completeness. [OpenStax College Algebra 2e, §1.2, The Negative Rule of Exponents](https://openstax.org/books/college-algebra-2e/pages/1-2-exponents-and-scientific-notation).

findings.quote: 2. Multiply exponents. The base is positive, so this rule applies.
findings.problem: Example 2 requires the power-of-a-power rule to rewrite both sides with base 2. Core Concept teaches equal-base comparison but never teaches how to simplify a power raised to another power. This rule is taught in Exponent Laws and Zero Powers, but this part gives no prerequisite reference.
findings.source: Content checklist L17 and L25; lesson-style-guide.md, Teaching completeness. [OpenStax Precalculus 2e, §4.6, Using Like Bases to Solve Exponential Equations](https://openstax.org/books/precalculus-2e/pages/4-6-exponential-and-logarithmic-equations).
